### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace contained exactly one of three alternative activities: A19 in about 32 in 100 cases (64 of 200 traces), A20 in about 28 in 100, and A25 in about 40 in 100, each appearing at most once per trace; the three never occurred together. In the later window, each of the three appears in only about 1 in 200 traces, so roughly 199 in 200 traces contain none of them. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL001, REL002, REL006]
- These three activities were embedded between the A27/A28 region and A29: in the earlier window each co-occurred with A27, A28 and A29 in about 28–40 in 100 cases (always after A27 and before A29, with a mixed order against A28), whereas in the later window these co-occurrences have practically vanished (about 1 in 200 traces). [REL003, REL004, REL005, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- The step distances show the inserted gap closing: A27 followed directly by A28 rose from about 54 in 100 cases to about 99 in 100; A28 followed directly by A29 rose from about 45 in 100 to about 98 in 100; and the typical distance from A27 to A29 shortened from three steps (about 94 in 100) to two steps (about 97 in 100). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- The successor profiles consolidated accordingly: A27's outgoing transitions went from A28 (about 53%), A25 (about 20%), A19 (about 13%) and A20 (about 10%) to almost only A28 (about 97%); A28's went from A29 (about 45%) plus A25, A19 and A20 (about 19%, 18% and 17%) to almost only A29 (about 98%). [DIR004, DIR005]
- A27, A28 and A29 themselves still occur in essentially every trace in both windows; A29's mean event position moved only slightly earlier (about 0.56 to 0.55 of the trace). [POS004, DIR004, DIR005]
- The apparent new successors of A19, A20 and A25 (A44, A08, A42) and their position statistics in the later window each rest on a single trace and should not be read as behaviour. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the block of three alternative activities A19, A20 and A25 — which in the earlier window was executed exactly once in every trace, inserted between the A27/A28 region and A29 — is no longer executed in the later window, leaving a direct A27 → A28 → A29 course. Participation of all three fell from 28–40% to about 0.5% on solid before-support (56–80 traces each); their co-occurrence with A27, A28 and A29 collapsed in pairs observed in all 200 traces of both windows; and the lag distributions contracted to direct succession exactly where the block used to sit. The screening flagged 27 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected without change, so the ensemble is unlikely to be a sampling artifact. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL005, REL009, REL010, REL012, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, DIR004, DIR005]

Limitations: the three activities still appear in one trace each, so complete removal versus extreme rarity cannot be distinguished; the single-trace successor profiles of A19, A20 and A25 cannot establish any replacement activities; and the many agreeing items largely describe one and the same trace behaviour rather than independent confirmations. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the block survives in a now very rare variant rather than having been dropped from the flow entirely. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
